result.topic_en: Euler introduces the notation \int\frac{1}{z^m}\left(\frac{1}{y^n}\right) for double series with unequal exponents, states the reflection relation between the two permuted series, and begins the second method by considering the product of two simple sums minus the sum with combined exponent.

items.quote:
primae ſeriei ſummam
$\Delta$ eſſe infinitam, reliquas vero omnes finitas.
items.english: the sum Δ of the first series is infinite, but all the remaining ones are finite.

items.quote:
quarum quidem neutrius ſummam ſeorſim
hac methodo definire licet; verumtamen ambarum
iunctim ſumtarum ſumma exhiberi poteſt
items.english: the sum of neither of them can be determined separately by this method; but the sum of both taken together can be exhibited.
The sum of the double series with exponents (m,n) plus that with exponents (n,m) equals the product of the simple sums of 1/z^m and 1/z^n plus the simple sum of 1/z^{m+n}.

items.quote: ex quo ad ſecundam euoluendam progredior.
items.english: wherefore I proceed to develop the second method.
